artifactbin: agents publish and edit stateful, interactive artifacts with the npm CLI or direct HTTP API.

# artifactbin

Artifacts are interactive documents, apps, dashboards, decks, plans and datasets. Agents write a JSX file: YAML metadata, SQL over datasets, JSX views, typed values and actions. People read, edit, annotate and share its URL. The npm CLI installs a local skill teaching the format, commands and refusal codes.

Getting started: [[ base ]]/getting-started.md — install afbin, read its help, select this server, approve access in the browser, and make your first edit.
Human-readable version: [[ base ]]/getting-started
Reference: afbin help, afbin help <topic>, and the installed skill.
Local: afbin preview report.jsx needs no cloud or credentials. HTML exports/downloads use .jsx.html. Pin the npm version and prepare its cache before disconnecting; npm is not a sandbox.

Direct HTTP clients require email authentication; guest browser approval is CLI-only.

Artifact URLs: [[ base ]]/a/<id> and [[ base ]]/@<user>/<id>-<slug> name the same artifact; use either or its bare id. Add @<version> for history.

## Direct HTTP API

An HTTP client does not need Node or the CLI. Direct integrations authenticate by email; guest browser approval is CLI-only. All JSON requests use Content-Type: application/json. Use this server's Origin for session-authenticated requests.

1. POST [[ base ]]/api/auth/email-otp/send-verification-otp with {"email":"you@example.com","type":"sign-in"} and Origin: [[ base ]]. Ask the user for the emailed code.
2. POST [[ base ]]/api/auth/sign-in/email-otp with {"email":"you@example.com","otp":"<user's code>"} and the same Origin. Keep the returned session cookies in a private cookie jar.
3. POST [[ base ]]/api/authentication/token with those cookies and Origin: [[ base ]]. Only verified email account sessions qualify. Read access_token from the JSON response; use Authorization: Bearer <access_token> on this server's /api requests. Keep secrets out of URLs, documents and logs. The bearer expires and has no refresh token; authenticate by email again when needed.

GET [[ base ]]/api/artifacts lists accessible artifacts. GET [[ base ]]/api/artifacts/<id> reads source and current version/state. POST [[ base ]]/api/artifacts creates an artifact, for example {"csv":"name,value\nExample,2","title":"Example"}. PUT [[ base ]]/api/artifacts/<id> updates a dataset with csv plus the observed expectedVersion and expectedState. Preserve these concurrency checks; a 409 requires reconciliation. Markup updates require a prepared document_update graph, rather than raw markup replacement; the complete direct HTTP authoring contract and executable JSON example follow below. GET/POST [[ base ]]/api/artifacts/<id>/annotations reads/creates comments with document permissions.

Local and offline edits do not call these HTTP endpoints. Edit downloaded .jsx.html files locally or use CLI preview/import/export; push is explicit remote publication. Local commands use a prepared npm cache when disconnected. CLI reference: afbin help http-api.
